                                                                                                                                         Paul McAllister
                                                                                                              3 years ago

                                                                                                                                           Lillian M Schettini - Copper is particularly unstable in
                                                                                                          lead glazes notoriously, which are very 'soft' in glaze
                                                                                                          terms, but really at stoneware temperatures, unless its
                                                                                             a very dry glaze or has some other material in it like
                                                                                                       Barium, its really not an issue as the copper will be
                                                                                        bound up in the glassy matrix. Not sure what kind of
                                                                                               ash glazes you have seen break down chemically after
                                                                                             a while. I really think this is a bit of a nonsense idea, I
                                                                                 mean I would be rather more worried about the fumes
                                                                                                     your car pump out which will get you before any glaze
                                                                                                               materials leaching out into your food! Its only with
                                                                                                                  certain foods anyhow.

                                                                                                   1 year ago

                                                                    Hey, I am sorry but I am in apprentice with glaze. Could you

                                                                                                            1 year ago

                                                                             Jessica LETACQ Hi, I am guessing they mean they
                                                                      dipped it three times in each firing type? I mean its
                                                                              three glaze tests each with a progressive test dipped
                                                                          once, twice and three times....but maybe I am
                                                                                     incorrect!



                                                                                        Bauke Van der Geest
                                                                               8 months ago

                                                                             Jessica LETACQ it's just the three above and on the
                                                                         bottom, so the three above are reduction fired, the
                                                                              three on the bottom in oxidation. Perhaps a Dutch way
                                                                                to describe 😀
                                                                                I'm amazed that there's so much difference with only
                                                                           the ash. Love it! Already made a Nuka but I will try this
                                                                 one to. Dank je wel!
